resources.string: Controller data stays on this phone. No account or Wi-Fi password storage. Update checks contact GitHub; you can turn automatic checks off.
Android 17 needs the “Nearby devices” permission before an app can talk to devices on the local network, including the softener and its setup network.
The permission was declined. Allow it under App info → Permissions → Nearby devices.
The module refused the local login. This can happen after it was paired with the vendor cloud app; setting up its Wi-Fi again with this app usually resets it.
Android blocked local network access. Allow “Nearby devices” for this app and turn off any VPN.
The Wi-Fi connection is not available.

This phone is not connected to a Wi-Fi network.
This Wi-Fi network has working Internet access, so it is not %1$s (the module’s setup network never does).
Connected to a Wi-Fi network without Internet access.
I checked in Android’s Wi-Fi settings that this phone is connected to %1$s.
Android only tells apps the Wi-Fi name if they have precise Location permission. This app uses it for nothing else and never reads your location. You can also skip this and confirm below.
Turn on Location so Android can show this app the Wi-Fi name, or confirm below.
Android did not reveal the network name. Confirm below if it is %1$s.

1. Unplug the softener, then plug it back in.
2. While the controller shows its model (for example “F136”), hold the Menu/OK button until it beeps. The controller now opens the “%1$s” network.
3. Tap “Open Wi-Fi networks” and join “%1$s”. If Android says the network has no Internet access, choose to stay connected.
4. Come back to this app.
That is the module’s own setup network. Enter your home Wi-Fi name.
Too long: %1$d bytes. The BroadLink setup packet carries at most %2$d (the official app has the same limit).
WPA passwords have at least %1$d characters.
WPA2 suits almost every router. If the module does not join, try WPA/WPA2.
The BL3372 only supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. Use your router’s 2.4 GHz network name; 5 GHz-only and WPA3-only networks will not work.
The name starts or ends with a space. Check that this is intended.
The name contains non-ASCII characters; it is sent as UTF-8.
The password contains non-ASCII characters. WPA passwords are normally plain ASCII; the module may reject it.
Sends the Wi-Fi name and password straight to the module over the %1$s connection. The BroadLink setup protocol is not encrypted, so do this close to the device and finish promptly.
Fill in your home Wi-Fi details (step 2).
The module acknowledged the settings (reply from %1$s).
Settings sent %1$d×. No acknowledgement came back, which many modules never send, so this alone does not mean failure.
Settings sent, and the %1$s connection dropped right after.
Watching %1$s… Once the module accepts the settings it reboots, its setup network disappears and it joins “%2$s”.
%1$s disappeared %2$d s after sending. The module has most likely rebooted and is now joining “%3$s”. Reconnect this phone to that network to find it.
This phone is still connected to %1$s after 90 s. The module may not have accepted the settings.

• Check the Wi-Fi name and password (both are case-sensitive).
• Make sure the router offers 2.4 GHz and is not WPA3-only.
• Try the security setting WPA/WPA2.
• Some BroadLink firmware fails with special characters in the password; a guest network with a letters-and-digits password can help.
• Put the controller back into Wi-Fi setup mode, reconnect and send again.
After the module has joined your Wi-Fi, connect this phone to your network. The app finds the module with BroadLink’s local discovery.
Connect this phone to your home Wi-Fi.
This phone is still on the setup network. Switch to your home Wi-Fi first.
Device on another VLAN or subnet?

Searches do not cross VLANs or routers. If the softener is on another network (for example an IoT VLAN), enter its IP address, or scan its subnet. Your firewall must allow UDP port 80 from this phone to the device.
No BroadLink device answered. The module can take a minute or two to join; search again. If it is on another VLAN, use the option above.
No BroadLink device answered at that address. Check the address and that your firewall allows UDP port 80 to it.
Enter an IPv4 address (e.g. 192.168.20.15) or a hostname that resolves on this network.
Reports itself as locked (local control disabled by the vendor app).
Looking for the device on its subnet…
This phone is not on Wi-Fi.
No answer from the device (last address %1$s).
Check that the softener is powered and on Wi-Fi. If it is on another VLAN, make sure UDP port 80 is allowed, or enter its new address.
Useful when the softener is on another VLAN and its address changed. Reserving a fixed address for it in your router avoids this.
Forget this device on this phone? The softener itself is not changed.

No registered profile matches controller code %1$s. Readings use the F79D fallback, verified only for code %2$d, and may be wrong. Comparing readings does not verify every command. Controls require your experimental opt-in.
The values below (for example hardness and regeneration time) match my controller’s display.
This identity matches the existing hardware-verified local profile.
The reported code is a protocol identity; it is not necessarily the product name printed on the valve.
Experimental controls enabled. Readings and commands remain unverified for this controller.
Module type %1$s has no supported Runxin transport. Controller commands are disabled.

After connection, the app reads the controller identity and loads a matching local profile. BL3372 type 0x520F with controller code 9 selects Runxin F79D. Other controller codes use an experimental fallback with controls locked until you opt in. An unknown BroadLink module type is unsupported.

Runxin publishes a dedicated Wi-Fi manual for F79A, F79B, F82A and F82B LCD variants. A Wi-Fi product listing does not establish compatibility with this app’s local commands. These product names are not automatically assigned protocol codes.

The official manual lists F105 and F136 variants, including F105AHW, F105BHW and F136BHW. Some functions need a Wi-Fi control board. It documents hardness, regeneration time, leakage limits, salt bookkeeping and vacation mode, but does not establish this app’s local field mappings.

Runxin also offers manual valves, filter valves, duplex systems and RS-485-equipped controllers. RS-485 support does not imply BL3372 Wi-Fi support. This app currently has no RS-485 transport or local profiles for those product families.

BroadLink describes product-specific profiles and control scripts in its official SDK. Sharing a brand or Wi-Fi chipset does not make commands interchangeable. This app uses the established Runxin BL3372 transport; it does not control BroadLink remotes, plugs, lights or gateways.
Guide reviewed on 4 October 2026. Source links open your browser and need Internet access. Automatic profile selection uses profiles bundled with the app.
Vacation mode is switched on the controller: while in service, hold ▼ (Down) for 6 seconds; do the same to end it.
Controls are locked for this controller.
Per the Midnight manual, enter the measured German hardness (°dH / nk°) × 10, e.g. 15 nk° → 150 mg/l.
The controller’s salt bookkeeping, not a measured salt level. Enter how much salt you added.
Pick a time when nobody uses water; the manual suggests 22:00–0:00.
SafeHOME closes the valve when water flows longer, or faster, than these limits (suspected pipe burst). 0 = off.
The softener regenerates immediately. It delivers no water during the first phase and only hard water afterwards, and uses salt and water. A full cycle takes a few hours.
Only available while the softener is in service. The app confirms that the valve has started moving.
%1$s saved and confirmed by the controller.
Regeneration started. The controller confirmed the valve is moving.
%1$s was sent, but the controller did not confirm the change. It may not accept this setting.
No reply while sending %1$s, and the change was not confirmed. Check the value before trying again.
Hungarian, unless the phone is set to English
Local control profiles: %1$d · Documentation entries: %2$d. Tap a model for its evidence and source. Documentation entries do not enable controls or identify a connected controller.
No matching documented model. The connected controller can still use experimental mode if its module is supported.
Automatically loaded for module 0x520F and reported code 9. Local command mapping verified by the public ypsilon-local project on a real F79D device; it is not manufacturer certification.
Named in the official LCD Wi-Fi manual directory. The full manual was not inspected. No proven local command mapping is available in this app; Wi-Fi alone does not establish compatibility.

The inspected F105/F136 manufacturer manual links this old model name to the listed product alias. It describes regeneration, hardness, leakage limits, salt bookkeeping and vacation mode. Some functions require a Wi-Fi board. No local command mapping is established for this variant.
Named in the official Runxin manual directory. Its individual manual and network interface have not been audited. No local command mapping is available in this app.

Checks contact GitHub for public release information. Downloads contact GitHub and its asset servers. No controller details or Wi-Fi credentials are sent. Controller setup and operation work without Internet.

This installation uses a different signing key, such as an Android Studio debug build. A release APK cannot update it. Install the official signed release separately; uninstalling this build removes its saved devices.
